To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the enhanced resonant active metasurface embedded with a nanostructure 2DEG of GaN HETM is capable of achieving an extremely large phase modulation of THZ waves, which is of great significance to the development of THZ application systems.

the large phase modulation of THZ waves can be addressed through an active and enhanced-resonant metamaterial structure embedded with the nanostructured two-dimensional electron gas (2-DEG) layer in GaN high electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) with a high speed.
the active and enhanced resonances of metamaterials are dynamically modulated by a nanostructured 3 nm 3D carrier gas of HEMT, leading to a large phase shift in the THz wave.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new THz phase modulation technique based on a dynamic active metamaterial structure.
the design and realization of a large phase modulation of THZ waves via an enhanced resonator active metamaterial.
the development of an active metamaterial-based phase modulator that can be applied in the THz regime.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper demonstrates that efficient phase modulation can be achieved by using a dynamic metamaterial structure with a nanostructured HEMT 2DEG embedded in an enhanced resonant metamater.

this work demonstrates that the phase shift of THz waves in a dynamic experiment can be efficiently modulated by a single layer of active metamaterials with a high modulation depth of greater than 100 °, which is the first time this has been achieved.

we demonstrate that a large phase shift of a THz wave can be achieved by a resonant metamaterial with an enhanced resonance mode embedded with the nanostructured two-dimensional electron gas (2D-EG) layer of a high electron mobility transistor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel THz phase shifter based on an active HEMT metamaterial.
we have developed a new concept of active metamaterials for the dynamic control of THz waves, which has a great potential in THz application fields.
the enhanced resonant metastructure with a nanostructured HEMT layer provides an efficient way for large phase modulation in THz systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase shift of THz waves in a metamaterial structure can be efficiently modulated by dynamically manipulating the resonance of the structure.
an active resonant metamaterial structure can provide an effective approach for the design of a large phase modulation THz modulator.
the active and enhanced resonator can be a promising candidate for realizing a fast phase modulator in the terahertz region.
